callouts.note: Each callout carries an .idle face (Scene 05) and an .act face (the hover/pressed state from Scenes 5.1, 5.2, 5.3, 5.3-follow). Row boxes, stage px: react (339,288.90) 205.54x88 -> act (339,284.78) 218.78x96.24; comment (339,431.06) 270.54x88 -> act 274.54 wide; bookmark (339,573.21) 279.23x83.69 -> act 287.23 wide; follow (339,711.06) 279.23x80 -> FOLLOWING 312 wide. Padding 8, gap 13.54, radius 8; label 32px, Regular idle / Bold hovered (the FOLLOW pill label stays Regular). Active icon art: react = same glyph rotated -7deg; comment = mirrored bubble, 80.25x72, overhanging the 72px slot to the right; bookmark = filled; follow = plus (44x44) -> tick (44x44). Figma's auto-layout reflows the column when a row grows; we keep row positions fixed and share an icon centre between the two faces instead, so nothing moves mid-scrub.

react-wall.note: Animated 4x5 wall of 20 looping reactions. Rebuild with tools/make-react-wall.py (2.6 MB vs the GIF's 7.5 MB, and cleaner — the GIF's 256-colour palette dithers the gradients). Pillow coalesces identical consecutive frames 70 -> 56 and folds their durations, so the loop still totals exactly 2330 ms; the script asserts this, because Pillow's WebP READER reports per-frame durations as None and will look like data loss. Rendered through 20 clipping cells built in buildDom (one each, all pointing at this one file, so one decode and all 20 stay frame-synced) which lets each cell stagger in on its own. The cells tile the image exactly, so at rest the composite is pixel-identical to the whole frame and emoji that overflow their cell (jack-in-the-box, NO sign) are not clipped. Background is opaque black — the same black as the stage — so no alpha is needed; if the stage ever stops being #000 this asset needs keying.

sat-merch-left.note: added to Scene 19 (1838:120893) 2026-07-29. Rotation is BAKED INTO THE ART, unlike the other four satellites — Figma reports only the rotated bbox for this node and un-rotating in PIL would resample the card. ending-frames.note: NOT a node export — tools/make-ending-frames.py. The s24 finale: an 8x8 sprite grid of the closing I.D. video (60 frames, resampled from the source's 24 fps to 12), swept by the timeline and positioned with a transform so one cell shows at a time. Cells are 1024x576 in the sheet and displayed full-bleed at 1920x1080 — the source is 1280x720, exactly the stage's 16:9. Frame 0 registers on #id-card / the encased #gold-card, which is what lets s24 hand over with a plain crossfade. 2.96 MB.
